speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm. To understand how long this has been going on, can you tell me when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of symptoms, especially with your history of heavy smoking and alcohol use. Have you noticed any pain in your right arm or shoulder, or any changes in reflexes when I test them?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of heavy smoking and significant weight loss, Multiple Sclerosis is highly unlikely for you. To differentiate between a peripheral nerve issue, a cervical spine problem, or a systemic malignancy, I need to examine your reflexes and check your blood work. Please extend your right arm while I test your biceps and triceps reflexes, and also REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, and Tumor_Markers.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature: 99.5°F (37.5°C), Blood_Pressure: 177/108 mmHg, Heart_Rate: 90/min, Respiratory_Rate: 17/min, Oxygen_Saturation: 98% on room air, Strength_Assessment: 2/5 strength in the right arm and 5/5 strength in the left arm, Sensory_Examination: Decreased sensation in the right arm, Reflexes: Normal, Coordination: Unaffected, Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Within normal limits, Hemoglobin: Within normal limits, Platelets: Within normal limits, Chest_X-ray: Findings: Mass noted at the apex of the right lung, CT_Chest: Findings: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing brachial plexus invasion.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the CT_Chest images showing the right lung apex mass for further evaluation of mediastinal and pleural involvement.
